predecessors.name: Northern Liang
predecessors.text: Dunhuang and the Jinchang commandery (Anxi/Guazhou side), where Li Gao rose in 400

successors.name: Northern Liang
successors.text: Dunhuang, Jinchang, Jiuquan and Liangning, Cliopatria's 407-409 shape

ledger.x: 400: Li Gao proclaims the Western Liang at Dunhuang.
401: Jiuquan and Liangning join Li Gao.

405: Li Gao moves the capital east to Jiuquan 'to apply more pressure on the Northern Liang'; he also allied with the Southern Liang, nominally submitted to Later Qin and sent tribute to Northern Wei.
421: the Northern Liang ends the Western Liang.

wars.name: Li Gao's rising against the Northern Liang
wars.outcome: Li Gao is acclaimed at Dunhuang and Jinchang in 400 and takes Jiuquan and Liangning in 401; the Northern Liang keeps Zhangye.

wars.name: Northern Liang conquest of the Western Liang
wars.outcome: Li Xin dies in battle outside Guzang in 420; Jiuquan falls in 420 and Dunhuang in 421, where Li Xun commits suicide.

certainty.note: The oases of Dunhuang, Jinchang and Jiuquan are named by commandery only; no frontier with the Northern Liang or the desert is given.
